g.text: IN PLAIN ENGLISH
At time t, count jobs currently executing on the same resource.
The count cannot exceed that resource's actual execution capacity.
Accepting another request does not make another worker available.
p(v)=q: stage v runs on resource q; k_q: simultaneous slots.
Each indicator is 1 between that job's start S and finish F, and 0 otherwise.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: WORKED RAP EXAMPLE
The shared source-render worker has k_q = 1.
Session A runs from 5,000 to 6,800 ms.
Session B is ready at 5,000 ms but must wait.
B then runs from 6,800 to 8,600 ms.
At t = 6,000: A counts as 1 and B as 0.
Total executing = 1, which satisfies capacity 1.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: Two executing jobs would exceed capacity 1
This models the protected render worker.
It does not claim the entire GPU can run only one task.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: WHAT THIS TELLS US
Concurrent requests can increase waiting without speeding up this shared stage. A different worker or lock
design could change capacity, but a larger admission limit alone does not establish that improvement.
